introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2025. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (code 0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A (Pure Mathematics, compulsory) and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B (Mechanics) OR SECTION C (Statistics and Probability). In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. If Section B is chosen, Section C may not be chosen, and the other way round. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Non-programmable electronic calculators and Mathematical Formulae booklets published by the GCE Board are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.

questions.corrige_markdown:
Use the double angle formulae $\cos2A=2\cos^2A-1$ and $\sin2A=2\sin A\cos A$.

$\dfrac{1+\cos2A}{\sin2A}=\dfrac{1+(2\cos^2A-1)}{2\sin A\cos A}=\dfrac{2\cos^2A}{2\sin A\cos A}=\dfrac{\cos A}{\sin A}=\cot A.$ $\blacksquare$

questions.enonce_markdown:
(ii)(a) The function $f$ is defined by $f(x)=3\sin x+2\cos x$, for $0\le x\le\pi$. Copy and complete the table below. *[3 marks]*

| $x$ | $0$ | $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ | $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ | $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ | $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$ | $\dfrac{5\pi}{6}$ | $\pi$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $f(x)$ | 2.0 |  |  |  |  | -1.7 |  |
(ii)(b) Taking 2 cm to represent $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ radians on the $x$-axis and 2 cm to represent 1 unit on the $y$-axis, draw the graph of $y=f(x)$ for $0\le x\le\pi$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Axes.** $x$-axis from $0$ to $\pi$: 12 cm in all (2 cm per $\pi/6$). $y$-axis from $-2$ to $4$: 12 cm in all (2 cm per unit), with the origin placed 4 cm above the bottom of the grid.

**Points to plot** (from the table), in centimetres from the origin, horizontally and vertically:

| $x$ | $0$ | $\pi/6$ | $\pi/3$ | $\pi/2$ | $2\pi/3$ | $5\pi/6$ | $\pi$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $f(x)$ | 2.0 | 3.2 | 3.6 | 3.0 | 1.6 | -0.2 | -2.0 |
| position (cm) | $(0,\ 4.0)$ | $(2,\ 6.4)$ | $(4,\ 7.2)$ | $(6,\ 6.0)$ | $(8,\ 3.2)$ | $(10,\ -0.4)$ | $(12,\ -4.0)$ |

Join the points with a **smooth curve**: it rises from $(0,2)$ to a maximum near $x\approx1.0$ (between $\pi/6$ and $\pi/2$, close to $\pi/3$), then decreases, crosses the $x$-axis at $x\approx2.55$ (just before $5\pi/6\approx2.62$) and ends at $(\pi,-2)$.

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(c) Using your graph, estimate the maximum value of $f(x)$. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
On the graph, the highest point of the curve is at $x\approx1.0$ rad (about $56^\circ$, slightly below $\pi/3$ and above $\pi/6$), with height about $3.6$.

**Maximum value of $f(x)\approx3.6$.**

(Exact value: $3\sin x+2\cos x=\sqrt{13}\cos(x-\alpha)$ with $\tan\alpha=\tfrac32$, so the maximum is $\sqrt{13}\approx3.61$, reached at $x=\arctan\tfrac32\approx0.98$ rad.)
